diagnostic_evidence.quote: \langle N(\mathcal{T}),N(\mathcal{T}') \rangle_{W^{*}} = \frac{\pi^{2}}{4}\sum_{i=1}^{n_{e}}\sum_{j=1}^{m_{e}}{k_{p}(c_{i},d_{j})\langle f_{i},g_{j}\rangle}\bigg\langle \sum_{\{T|f_{i}\ \mathrm{edge\ of}\ T\}}{n_{T,f_{i}}}, \sum_{\{T|g_{j}\ \mathrm{edge\ of}\ T\}}{n_{T,g_{j}}}\bigg\rangle

Given two triangulations $\mathcal{T},\mathcal{T}'$, one may check the resulting scalar product of $N(\mathcal{T}),N(\mathcal{T}') \in W^{*}$ of \cref{NC_delta} agrees with \cref{NC_disc_met} derived in \cite{NCpaper}.

issues.failure_explanation: The discrete normal cycle decomposition in (13) assigns a prefactor of $\pi$ to both the cylindrical and boundary spherical components. Computing the inner product $\langle N(\mathcal{T}), N(\mathcal{T}') \rangle_{W^*}$ from (13) produces prefactors of $\pi^2$ for both terms, which is 4 times larger than the $\frac{\pi^2}{4}$ prefactors in the established metric of Theorem 1 (\cref{NC_disc_met}), contradicting the explicit assertion that the scalar product from \cref{NC_delta} agrees with \cref{NC_disc_met}. Furthermore, \cref{realembedding} in (16) assigns prefactor $\pi$ to the cylindrical component and $\frac{\pi}{2}$ to the boundary component, contradicting (13) and distorting the relative weighting between the cylindrical and boundary components by a factor of 4.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the prefactor $\pi$ with $\frac{\pi}{2}$ for both components in \cref{NC_delta} and \cref{realembedding}, and ensure the edge coordinates and edge centres are consistently indexed.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete functional representation $N(\mathcal{T})$ in \cref{NC_delta} and its embedding $F(N(\mathcal{T}))$ in \cref{realembedding} do not reproduce the discrete normal cycle metric of Theorem 1 as claimed, and the components in (16) have mismatched relative weights.
issues.title: Inconsistent and erroneous prefactors in the discrete normal cycle delta decomposition
issues.why_classification: Correcting the scalar prefactors from $\pi$ to $\frac{\pi}{2}$ is a routine local adjustment that immediately restores exact agreement with Theorem 1 and leaves the algorithm and theoretical guarantees intact without requiring new architecture or weakening results.
